newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Thursday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Volume dropped to 1.1 billion yuan from 1.6 billion on Wednesday, with the seven-day contract the most active.
Traders said the rates went up today, with less money being lent out but borrowing remaining at Wednesday's level.
Trading was dull, with most institutions reducing their business with the approach of the year-end, they said.
Traders said that, with the central bank continuing to stress a tight money policy, market rates were likely to remain firm in the short term.
State banks, which acted as major lenders in the last two months, have reduced their lending, which was likely to change the balance of supply and demand, they said.
